subject: Proof of Patch Throughput and Retention — Calyx Bank SIG follow-up
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Nguyen <security@calyxbank.com>, Rajeev Singh <techops@calyxbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Proof of Patch Throughput and Retention — Calyx Bank SIG follow-up

Hi Lisa / Rajeev —

Per our SIG review this morning, attaching the VM artifacts you requested so your compliance team can validate our scan cadence and SLA posture. This package is intended to show both our operational tempo (how fast we close CVEs) and our evidence retention for audit. Items attached: 1) 20260818_scan_snapshot.csv (last three full scans across prod & staging), 2) patch_manifest_Q2_2026.pdf (owners / rollouts), 3) cve_closure_timeline.csv (CVE -> patch -> close timestamps), 4) retention_matrix_2026.xlsx (retention policy by artifact).

Quick summary:
- Critical CVEs: target 7-day remediation SLA; current median time-to-close for criticals in last 90 days = 5 days.
- High CVEs: target 30-day remediation SLA; current median = 12 days.
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated full scans for external-facing fleet, daily incremental for container images.
- Evidence retention: 24 months for scan results, 7 years for audit artifacts (policy-exempt items flagged).

Ask: please confirm if this packet is sufficient for your SIG reviewer, or if you need a signed attestation (we can provide an executive-signed PDF) or raw scan exports in NDJSON. If helpful, Monica can join a short call to walk through the CSV columns.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Account Security (Sales enablement)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: 20260818_scan_snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB), patch_manifest_Q2_2026.pdf (PDF, 128KB), cve_closure_timeline.csv (CSV, 18KB), retention_matrix_2026.xlsx (XLSX, 56KB)

From: Lisa Nguyen <security@calyxbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajeev Singh <techops@calyxbank.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proof of Patch Throughput and Retention — Calyx Bank SIG follow-up

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick packet. A couple of clarifying items from our SIG reviewer before we close this out:

1) In cve_closure_timeline.csv we see an entry (CVE-2026-1144) flagged as "closed" but the remediation patch is listed in a different manifest row with a deployment date after the close date. Can you confirm whether the closure reflects an applied patch or an accepted compensating control?

2) For your "daily incremental" container scans — do you keep immutable scan artifacts tied to image digests for at least 24 months, or just the aggregated reports? We need tamper-evident proof for a sample of 3 images.

3) The retention_matrix_2026.xlsx has an entry that suggests "policy-exempt items flagged" — can you outline the process and approval path for exemptions? We need an audit trail.

If you can point us to the NDJSON exports for the three sample images and clarify the CVE-1144 row, we can finalize the SIG attestation this week.

Best,
Lisa Nguyen
Head of Security Governance
Calyx Bank

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Nguyen <security@calyxbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proof of Patch Throughput and Retention — Calyx Bank SIG follow-up

Thanks Lisa — I can take these. Quick answers and next steps inline below.

On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 11:20 AM Lisa Nguyen <security@calyxbank.com> wrote:
> 1) In cve_closure_timeline.csv we see an entry (CVE-2026-1144) flagged as "closed" but the remediation patch is listed in a different manifest row with a deployment date after the close date. Can you confirm whether the closure reflects an applied patch or an accepted compensating control?

Right: CVE-2026-1144 was initially mitigated via a network ACL and temporary process isolation on 2026-07-14 (compensating control), recorded as a closure in our triage log. The permanent patch rolled out to the affected fleet on 2026-07-27 (deployment date). We should have been clearer in the timeline CSV — closure column currently reflects the triage/mitigation milestone, not necessarily final patch deployment. I've attached a corrected row (included in the NDJSON export link below) that distinguishes "mitigation" vs "patch_deployed" timestamps.

> 2) For your "daily incremental" container scans — do you keep immutable scan artifacts tied to image digests for at least 24 months, or just the aggregated reports? We need tamper-evident proof for a sample of 3 images.

We retain signed scan artifacts for container images for 24 months. For each image digest we keep an export (NDJSON) with verifier hashes and a signature from our integrity vendor (J. Morales / integrity-scans@example.com). I will upload the three requested sample NDJSON files to the shared drive and provide sha256 sums. Expect those by EOD.

> 3) The retention_matrix_2026.xlsx has an entry that suggests "policy-exempt items flagged" — can you outline the process and approval path for exemptions? We need an audit trail.

Exemptions are handled by our Risk Committee. We maintain an approvals log in Confluence; exemptions are documented with a ticket (PRJ-SEC-####) and an approving manager and legal sign-off when required. I've attached a one-page flow summary and a link to the Confluence approvals list in the drive folder.

Next steps (action items):
- I will upload corrected NDJSON exports for the three sample images + sha256 sums (by 2026-08-19 18:00 PDT).
- Kimberly will provide an executive attestation template if Calyx needs a signed PDF.
- Naomi will confirm retention SLA language and provide the doc hash chain for one of the shipped artifacts.

If it's helpful, we can do a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow morning to walk the SIG reviewer through the NDJSON format.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Sr. Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: corrected_row_CVE-2026-1144.ndjson (NDJSON, 4KB)

From: Lisa Nguyen <security@calyxbank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proof of Patch Throughput and Retention — Calyx Bank SIG follow-up

Monica / Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarifications. I reviewed the corrected NDJSON row and the sample artifacts; the sha256 sums matched and the signed scan artifacts include the vendor signature chain we required. The distinction between "mitigation" and "patch_deployed" in the updated timeline is clear — that resolves our CVE-2026-1144 question.

One remaining ask: for our SIG attestation we need one signed executive statement that references the following bullet items explicitly: (a) scan cadence and retention policy (weekly/daily and 24 months), (b) CVE remediation SLAs (7/30 days for critical/high) and current median times, and (c) the exemption approval process (Risk Committee + ticketing reference). Can you send a short (1-page) executive-signed PDF that we can attach to the SIG submission? If you can get that by EOD Monday (2026-08-23), we will mark this evidence packet as complete.

If you prefer, I can also accept an emailed confirmation from your legal contact with the same content.

Thanks again — we look forward to closing this.

Lisa Nguyen
Head of Security Governance
Calyx Bank
